questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Consider the statements
In a semi conductor
(A) There are no free electrons at $0K$.
(B) There are no free electrons at any temperature
(C) The number of free electrons increases with temperature,
(D) The number of free electrons is less than that in a conductor.
options: B,C,D are true but A is false
A,B,C are true but D is false
A,C,D are true but B is false.
A,B,C and D are all true.
questions.solution:
In a semiconductor, at $0K$ all the electrons are in the valence band and no electrons are there in the conduction band. At $0K$ there are no free electrons but the number of electrons increases with the increase in temperature. As the temperature increases electrons gain kinetic energy, thus, breaks the covalent bonds and move to conduction band as the result number of free electrons and holes increases.The number of free electrons are less as they form a covalent bonds due to which lattice structure is created.

So,& A,C,D are true but B is false.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Output of following logic circuit is
questions.solution:
In the given circuit,& the outputs of all three $OR$ gates is given to the input of $AND$ gate.

Inputs to the first $OR$ gate are $\overset{¯}{A}$ and B as a $NOT$ gate in between& the input from A$. Similarly, inputs to second $OR$ gate are $\overset{¯}{A}$ and $\overset{¯}{C}$. And to third $OR$, inputs are B and $\overset{¯}{C}$.

We know the output of an $OR$ gate is the sum of inputs. Then, the outputs of the three $OR$gates are& \left(\overset{¯}{A} + B\right), \left(\overset{¯}{A} + \overset{¯}{C}\right)$ and $\left(B + \overset{¯}{C}\right).

Now, we know that the output of the$AND$ gate is the multiplication of the inputs. Therefore, the output of logic circuit is $Y = $\left(\overset{¯}{A} + B\right)\cdot \left(\overset{¯}{A} + \overset{¯}{C}\right)$\cdot $\left(B + \overset{¯}{C}\right)$.

questions.q: The current gain for a transistor working as common base amplifier is 0.96. If the emitter current is $7.2 \mathrm{ mA}$, then the base current is
questions.solution:
Given, current gain, $\alpha=0.96$
Emitter current, $I_E=7.2 \mathrm{ mA}=7.2 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{ A}$
We know that, $\begin{aligned}\alpha$& =I_C / I_E \\
\Rightarrow \quad I_C & =$\alpha \times$ I_E=0.96 $\times7.2 \times10^{-3} \mathrm{ A}=6.91 \times10^{-3} \mathrm{ A}\\
\text{ Also, }$ I_E & =I_C+I_B \\
\Rightarrow \quad I_B & =I_E-I_C=(7.2-6.91) $\times10^{-3} \mathrm{ A}\\ \text{$ and $} =0.29 \times10^{-3} \mathrm{ A}=0.29 \mathrm{ mA}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If current in diode is five times that in $R_1$ and breakdown voltage of diode is $6 \mathrm{ V}$, find the value of $R$ ?
questions.solution:
Given that, $R_{\mathrm{l}}=1 \mathrm{k} \Omega$, Zener breakdown voltage $V_z=6 \mathrm{~V}$ Let $I_1 and I_z$ be the current passing through $R_1$ and Zener diode, then using equation, $I_1=\frac{V_z}{R_1}=\frac{6}{1000} \mathrm{~A}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a \(p\)-type semiconductor the donor level is at \(50 \mathrm{meV}\) above the valence band. To produce one electron, the maximum wavelength of light photon required is (Planck's constant, \(h=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}\) and speed of light in vacuum, \(c=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}\) )
questions.solution:
Given,
\(p\)-type semiconductor donor energy level,
\(E=50 \mathrm{meV}=50 \times 10^{-3} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \mathrm{~V}\)
Planck's constant, \(h=6.6 \times 10^{-34} \mathrm{Js}\)
speed of light in vacuum, \(c=3 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}\)
Now, for the maximum wavelength of light photon's required \((p)\).
According to the Planck's quantum theory,
\(\therefore \quad E=h v \Rightarrow E=\frac{h c}{\lambda} \quad\left[\because v=\frac{c}{\lambda}\right]\)
Putting the given values, we get
\(50 \times 10^{-3} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}=\frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{\lambda}\)
\(\begin{aligned}
\lambda & =\frac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{50 \times 10^{-3} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-19}} \\
& =\frac{6.6 \times 3 \times 10^{-34} \times 10^8}{5 \times 16 \times 10^{-22}}=\frac{6.6 \times 3 \times 10^{-4}}{5 \times 16} \\
& =2.475 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~m} \\
\text{or } \lambda & =24.75 \times 10^{-6}=24.75 \mu \mathrm{m}
\end{aligned}\)
Hence, the maximum wavelength of light photon required is \(24.8 \mu \mathrm{m}\).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a transistor circuit, when the base current is increased by 50 micro-amperes keeping the collector voltage fixed at 2 volts, the collector current increases by $1 \mathrm{ mA}$. The current gain of the transistor is
questions.solution:
Increase in base current $\Delta$ I_b=50 \mu $\mathrm{A}$ Increase in collector current $\Delta I_c=1 \mathrm{ mA}$
Current gain $\beta=\frac{\Delta I_c}{\Delta I_b}=\frac{1 \times 10^{-3}}{50 \times 10^{-6}}=\frac{10^3}{50}=20$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A common emitter transistor amplifier has a current gain of 50. If the load resistance is $4 \mathrm{k} \Omega$ and input resistance is $500 \Omega$, the voltage gain of the amplifier is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} \beta=50, R_L=4 \mathrm{k} \Omega& =4000 \Omega \\
R_i & =500 \Omega \\
\beta& =\frac{I_c}{I_b}
\end{aligned}$ Voltage gain of amplifier $\begin{aligned}& =\frac{\text{ output voltage }}{\text{ input voltage }}=\frac{I_c \times R_L}{I_b \times R_i}\\
& =\beta\left(\frac{R_L}{R_i}\right)=\frac{50 \times 4000}{500}=400
\end{aligned}
$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: While a collector to emitter voltage is constant in a transistor, the collector current changes by 8.2 mA when the emitter current changes by $8.3 \mathrm{ mA}$. The value of forward current ratio is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \Delta I_c=8.2 \mathrm{ mA} \\ & \qquad \Delta I_c=8.3 \mathrm{ mA} \\ & \text{ Base current } \Delta I_b=\Delta I_c-\Delta I_c=8.3-8.2=0.1 \mathrm{ mA} \\ & \therefore \text{ Forward current ratio }=\frac{\Delta I_c}{\Delta I_b}=\frac{8.2}{0.1}=82\end{aligned}$
